# 1 Clement Chapter 20 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

### Theological and Literary Significance
Chapter 20 is the rhetorical masterpiece of 1 Clement and one of the most beautiful passages in all Ante-Nicene literature. It is a cosmic meditation — Clement surveys the entire created order and finds in each element a model of peaceful, harmonious obedience to God's commands:

- **Heavens** (v.1): day and night in harmony
- **Astronomical bodies** (v.2): sun, moon, stars in ordered orbits
- **Earth** (v.3): seasons producing food without dissent
- **Abyss and underworld** (v.4): even chaos is ordered
- **Ocean** (vv.5-6): the sea restrained by God's word (Job 38:11)
- **The far ocean and beyond** (v.7): even the unknown is ordered
- **Seasons** (v.8): peaceful succession
- **Winds and springs** (v.9): natural cycles and life-giving waters
- **Smallest creatures** (v.10): even the tiny live in peace

The argument culminates in v.11: the God who orders ALL things has shown his goodness "most abundantly" to Christians — who therefore have every reason to live in the harmony they have been given.

### Stoic Influence
The vision of cosmic *harmonia* is deeply indebted to Stoic cosmology, where the *logos* (rational principle) orders all things. Clement Christianizes this: the Sovereign Lord (*despotēs*) is the source of order, and his commands (*prostagmata*) hold everything in place.

### "Dancing Stars" / "Choir of Stars"
*Chorous* (v.2): The Greek word means both "choir" and "dance." The stars perform a cosmic dance/chorus. SOPHIA retains "choir of stars" as it captures both dimensions and was the standard image in Hellenistic cosmology.

### Key Translation Debates
- v.9 "breasts" vs. "life-giving water": The Greek *mastous* = breasts. Clement uses the nursing-mother image for springs feeding humanity. EMET preserves this literally; PNEUMA softens it; SOPHIA retains it as a vivid, intentional metaphor.
- v.11 "great Creator" vs. "great Craftsman": *dēmiourgos* = craftsman/maker/creator. SOPHIA uses "Craftsman" to distinguish from *ktistēs* (creator) used elsewhere.

---

## Chapter 20

**20:1** The heavens, moving under his governance, are subject to him in peace. Day and night run the course appointed by him, not hindering each other.

**20:2** The sun and moon and the choir of stars revolve in harmony through their appointed courses according to his ordinance, without any one transgressing his command.

**20:3** The earth, bearing fruit in fulfillment of his will at the proper seasons, brings forth food in abundance for men and beasts and all the living things upon it, not dissenting and altering none of his decrees.

**20:4** The unsearchable depths of the abyss and the inexpressible regions of the lower world are governed by the same ordinances.

**20:5** The basin of the boundless sea, gathered together by his workmanship into its reservoirs, does not pass beyond the barriers set around it, but does as he commanded it;

**20:6** For he said: "Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you." [Job 38:11]

**20:7** The impassable ocean and the worlds beyond it are regulated by the same decrees of the Master.

**20:8** The seasons of spring and summer and autumn and winter succeed each other in peace.

**20:9** The stations of the winds complete their proper courses without failure. The ever-flowing springs, made for enjoyment and for health, offer without fail their life-giving breasts for the sustenance of men.

**20:10** The smallest of living creatures come together in peace and concord.

**20:11** All these things the great Craftsman and Sovereign Lord of all willed to exist in peace and concord, bestowing his bounty on all things, but most abundantly upon us who have fled for refuge to his mercies through our Lord Jesus Christ,

**20:12** to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever. Amen.

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
